industries.rationale: The bill expands litigation procedures, jurisdictional reach, and limits defenses in civil claims, directly affecting law firms handling art recovery and international litigation.

bill.plainSummary: This bill removes the 2026 deadline for filing lawsuits to recover art and property stolen during the Holocaust, allowing claims to be filed indefinitely as long as they are brought within six years of discovering the item. The bill also blocks certain legal defenses, such as arguments that too much time has passed or that U.S. courts should defer to foreign laws, for both current and future cases.

bill.title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States providing that the rights protected and extended by the Constitution are the rights of natural persons only.
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
bill.policyArea: Civil Rights and Liberties, Minority Issues

industries.rationale: The amendment would subject banks and financial firms to new constitutional limits on political spending and strip them of constitutional rights currently recognized for corporations.
Technology companies would lose constitutional protections as corporate entities and face new restrictions on election-related expenditures and contributions.
Oil, gas, and coal companies would be subject to campaign finance limits and lose constitutional rights currently available to corporate entities.
Pharmaceutical and device manufacturers would face new restrictions on political spending and lose constitutional protections as artificial entities.
Law firms and lobbying organizations would operate under new campaign finance regulations and potentially altered constitutional frameworks for corporate clients.
Media corporations would lose constitutional rights as artificial entities, potentially affecting their ability to make election-related expenditures and editorial decisions.

bill.plainSummary: This proposed constitutional amendment would establish that only individual human beings—not corporations or other artificial entities—hold rights under the Constitution. It would require all levels of government to regulate or limit campaign contributions and spending, including candidates' own funds, to ensure equal political access regardless of wealth. The amendment would also mandate public disclosure of all permitted contributions and prevent courts from treating campaign spending as protected speech under the First Amendment.

bill.title: Safe Schools Improvement Act
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.

industries.rationale: The bill imposes new policy, reporting, and grievance-procedure obligations on local educational agencies and state education systems.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would require states to ensure that local school districts adopt policies prohibiting bullying and harassment of students based on race, color, national origin, disability, religion, sex (including sexual orientation, gender identity, and intersex traits). School districts would need to notify students and parents annually about these policies, establish complaint procedures, and publicly report data on bullying incidents. The Department of Education would evaluate anti-bullying programs every two years, and the National Center for Education Statistics would collect nationwide data on these incidents.

plain.whoItTouches: School districts, and children in them. Children, and the adults responsible for them.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would admit most of the current District of Columbia as the 51st state, called Washington, Douglass Commonwealth, with two senators and one representative in Congress. A small federal district containing the Capitol, White House, Supreme Court, and nearby monuments would remain as the seat of the federal government. The bill sets up a transition process for DC laws, courts, contracts, and obligations to continue under state authority, and creates a commission to manage the shift to statehood.

districtAwards.description: THE PURPOSE OF THIS AWARD IS TO FUND A FY 2022-2023 FEDERAL STATE PARTNERSHIP NORTHEAST CORRIDOR PROGRAM GRANT FOR THE HUDSON TUNNEL PROJECT (THE PROJECT OR HTP) TO HELP ACHIEVE THE GOALS IDENTIFIED IN THE NOTICE OF FUNDING OPPORTUNITY FOR PROJECTS LOCATED ON THE NORTHEAST CORRIDOR FOR THE FEDERAL-STATE PARTNERSHIP FOR INTERCITY PASSENGER RAIL GRANTS PROGRAM, 87 FED. REG. 79421, DECEMBER 27, 2022 THAT SOLICITED APPLICATIONS FOR FEDERAL FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE. THE FSP-NEC PROJECT CONSISTS OF THREE ELEMENTS: 1) THE CONSTRUCTION OF A NEW HUDSON RIVER TUNNEL BETWEEN NEW YORK AND NEW JERSEY  2) THE REHABILITATION OF THE EXISTING NORTH RIVER TUNNEL UNDER THE HUDSON RIVER  AND 3) LONG ISLAND RAIL ROAD (LIRR) EMERGENCY SERVICES BUILDING (ESB) UTILITY RELOCATION EARLY WORK ASSOCIATED WITH THE SEPARATELY FUNDED HUDSON YARDS CONCRETE CASING SECTION THREE (3) PROJECT. DELIVERABLES FOR THE PROJECT INCLUDE A PROJECT MANAGEMENT PLAN (PMP), FINAL DESIGN SET(S), A REAL ESTATE ACQUISITION MANAGEMENT PLAN (RAMP), CONTRACTOR PROPOSALS AND EXECUTED CONTRACTS, CONTRACTOR BUY AMERICA CERTIFICATION, AND A CONTRACTOR SAFETY PLAN.THE INTENDED BENEFICIARY AS A RESULT OF THIS PROJECT IS THE NATIONAL RAILROAD PASSENGER CORPORATION (AMTRAK).

APPLICATION PURPOSE: THE PURPOSE IS TO CONSTRUCT THE SECOND AVENUE SUBWAY PHASE 2 PROJECT.; ACTIVITIES PERFORMED: THE PROJECT INCLUDES THE CONSTRUCTION OF THREE NEW STATIONS TRACTION POWER SUBSTATIONS SIGNAL TRACK COMMUNICATION SYSTEMS AND STATION ARCHITECTURAL ELEMENTS AND FACILITIES.; EXPECTED OUTCOMES: THE SECOND AVENUE SUBWAY (SAS) PHASE 2 PROJECT (PROJECT) IS A PLANNED TWO-TRACK 1.76-MILE HEAVY RAIL SUBWAY EXTENSION ALONG THE EAST SIDE OF MANHATTAN. IT WILL CONNECT THE NORTHERN END OF PHASE 1 AT 105TH STREET TO THE 125TH STREET STATION OF THE LEXINGTON AVENUE LINE AND TERMINATE WEST OF THE INTERSECTION OF MALCOLM X BOULEVARD AND 125TH STREET.; INTENDED BENEFICIARIES: COMMUTERS ALONG MANHATTANS EAST SIDE AND USERS OF THE MTA SUBWAY SYSTEM.; SUBRECIPIENT ACTIVITIES: THERE ARE NO SUB-RECIPIENT ACTIVITIES WITH THIS AWARD.

APPLICATION PURPOSE: THE PURPOSE IS TO CONSTRUCT THE HUDSON TUNNEL PROJECT (HTP).; ACTIVITIES PERFORMED: THE HTP INCLUDES THREE ELEMENTS: 1) THE CONSTRUCTION OF A NEW HUDSON RIVER TUNNEL BETWEEN NEW YORK AND NEW JERSEY; 2) THE REHABILITATION OF THE EXISTING NORTH RIVER TUNNEL UNDER THE HUDSON RIVER; AND 3) LONG ISLAND RAIL ROAD (LIRR) EMERGENCY SERVICES BUILDING (ESB) UTILITY RELOCATION EARLY WORK ASSOCIATED WITH THE SEPARATELY FUNDED HUDSON YARDS CONCRETE CASING SECTION 3 PROJECT.; EXPECTED OUTCOMES: THE PURPOSE OF THE HTP IS TO PRESERVE THE CURRENT FUNCTIONALITY OF AMTRAKS NORTHEAST CORRIDOR (NEC) SERVICE AND NJ TRANSITS COMMUTER RAIL SERVICE BETWEEN NEW JERSEY AND PSNY BY REPAIRING THE DETERIORATING NORTH RIVER TUNNEL; AND TO STRENGTHEN THE NECS RESILIENCY TO SUPPORT RELIABLE SERVICE BY PROVIDING REDUNDANT CAPABILITY UNDER THE HUDSON RIVER FOR AMTRAK AND NJ TRANSIT NEC TRAINS BETWEEN NEW JERSEY AND PSNY. THESE IMPROVEMENTS MUST BE ACHIEVED WHILE MAINTAINING UNINTERRUPTED COMMUTER AND INTERCITY RAIL SERVICE AND BY OPTIMIZING THE USE OF EXISTING INFRASTRUCTURE. AT THE COMPLETION OF THE HTP THE NEC WOULD HAVE FOUR TRACKS (TWO IN THE NEW HUDSON TUNNEL AND TWO IN THE NORTH RIVER TUNNEL) BETWEEN NEW YORK AND NEW JERSEY UNDER THE HUDSON RIVER. NO CHANGES TO PSNY PLATFORMS OR PLATFORM TRACKS ARE PROPOSED AS PART OF THE HTP SINCE PSNY IS OUTSIDE OF THE HTP PROJECT AREA THEREFORE THE CURRENT OPERATIONAL CAPACITY OF PSNY WILL BE MAINTAINED AT THE LEVEL IT IS TODAY.; INTENDED BENEFICIARIES: THE HTP WILL ALLOW MULTIPLE NJ TRANSIT RAIL SERVICES THROUGHOUT THE STATE TO FEED INTO AND UTILIZE THE TUNNEL AND PSNY. THESE IMPORTANT RAIL CONNECTIONS FACILITATE THE MOVEMENT OF OVER 200000 TRAIN PASSENGERS TRIPS PER DAY BETWEEN NEW YORK AND NEW JERSEY.; SUBRECIPIENT ACTIVITIES: GDC DOES NOT HAVE ANY SUB-RECIPIENTS.

THE PROJECT INCLUDES FINAL DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION TO COMPREHENSIVELY REHABILITATE 19 MILES OF THE AMTRAK-OWNED HELL GATE LINE CONNECTING NEW YORK PENN STATION AND NEW ROCHELLE, NEW YORK. BENEFITS TO AMTRAKS INTERCITY SERVICES FROM THE PROJECT INCLUDE UPGRADED SIGNAL SYSTEMS, REHABILITATION OF FOUR BRIDGES, CONSTRUCTION OF FOUR NEW INTERLOCKINGS AND FIVE NEW POWER SUBSTATIONS, AND UPGRADES TO TWO EXISTING SUBSTATIONS, AND TRACK REHABILITATION. ADDITIONAL PROJECT COMPONENTS INCLUDE AN EXPANSION TO THE NEW ROCHELLE YARD. THE PROJECT WILL RESTORE THE HELL GATE LINE TO A STATE OF GOOD REPAIR AND ALLOW THE INTRODUCTION OF NEW METRO-NORTH RAILROAD (MNR) COMMUTER RAIL SERVICE OVER THE HELL GATE LINE CONNECTING TO PENN STATION NEW YORK. THE REHABILITATION AND REPLACEMENT OF ASSETS ON THE HELL GATE LINE WILL REVERSE DECADES-LONG UNDERINVESTMENT IN INTERCITY PASSENGER RAIL INFRASTRUCTURE. THE PROJECT WILL INSTALL A MODERN SIGNAL SYSTEM, REHABILITATE BRIDGES, INCREASE POWER, AND UPGRADE SIX MILES OF THE LINE INTO A FOUR-TRACK RAILROAD, IMPROVING OPERATIONAL FLEXIBILITY AS WELL AS ON-TIME PERFORMANCE AND RELIABILITY FOR 40,000 INTERCITY RAIL PASSENGERS THAT RELY ON THE LINE TODAY WHILE ALSO PREPARING THE NORTHEAST CORRIDOR (NEC) FOR INCREASED SERVICE LEVELS AND HIGH-SPEED RAIL SERVICE.
